questions.stem: A square-based pyramid has a base side of 6 cm and a vertical height of 10 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Base area = 6^2 = 36 cm squared. V = (1/3) x 36 x 10 = 120 cm cubed. A common error is forgetting the 1/3, which gives 360.

questions.stem: A cone has radius 7 cm and height 15 cm. What is its volume in terms of pi?
questions.explanation: V = (1/3) pi r^2 h = (1/3) x pi x 49 x 15 = (1/3) x 735 pi = 245 pi cm cubed.

questions.stem: A cone has volume 150 pi cm cubed and radius 5 cm. What is the height?
questions.explanation: V = (1/3) pi r^2 h. So 150 pi = (1/3) pi (25) h. Multiply both sides by 3: 450 pi = 25 pi h. Divide by pi: 450 = 25h, so h = 18 cm.

questions.stem: A frustum is made by removing a small cone (radius 3 cm, height 6 cm) from a large cone (radius 9 cm, height 18 cm). What is the volume of the frustum in terms of pi?
questions.explanation: Large cone: V = (1/3) pi (81)(18) = 486 pi. Small cone: V = (1/3) pi (9)(6) = 18 pi. Frustum = 486 pi - 18 pi = 468 pi cm cubed.

questions.stem: A cylinder and a cone have the same radius and height. The cylinder has volume 600 cm cubed. What is the volume of the cone?
questions.explanation: A cone has exactly 1/3 the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height. Cone volume = 600 / 3 = 200 cm cubed.
